title: sambucus canadensis f. acutiloba
intro: Sambucus canadensis f. acutiloba, commonly known as American elderberry, is a deciduous shrub native to eastern North America, characterized by its distinctive, sharply-toothed leaves and clusters of small, fragrant flowers that turn into dark purple berries. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for centuries, and its health benefits include anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help alleviate symptoms of colds and flu, as well as reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and certain cancers. The therapeutic actions of Sambucus canadensis f. acutiloba include immunomodulation, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory effects, which contribute to its use in treating respiratory and gastrointestinal issues. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and anthocyanins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and are also found in its berries, flowers, and leaves.
